knowledge_point.title: Integrating a Rational Function Using Natural Logarithms

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=2 t^{2} + 1.$ Then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}=4t\,⟹\,\frac{1}{4}\text{d}u=t\,\text{d}t.
$$

We can solve the required integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{-16t}{2 t^{2} + 1}\,\text{d}t & =-16\int \frac{1}{2 t^{2} + 1}\cdot t\,\text{d}t \\  & =-16\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \frac{1}{4}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-4\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-4\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+K \\  & =-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(2 t^{2} + 1)+K\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: Each real connected interval where the displayed denominator is nonzero; logarithms of absolute values. For the positive quadratic blank the domain is all real numbers.

checks.purpose: valid exact real positive log(abs) equivalent
